page.layout: One column of running text, with the title "De meritis operum." centred above the last passage. The catchword stands alone at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Fidei secretum & mysterium paucis manifestandum contendunt Basilidiani, Papistæ.
Fidem esse solam & nudam Euangelij cognitionem, quæ bona opera velut fructus adiuncta non habeat, docent Gnostici.
Opera bona à fide uti rem illi repugnantem, separant Simoniaci, Basilidiani, Libertini.
Ab operibus bonis, quæ Lege Dei præscribuntur, liberatos nos esse, eúmque esse fidei Christianæ fructum, dicunt Archontici, Antitactæ, Valesii.
Opera omnia bona Lege Dei præcepta, ne-gant nobis Christianis sectanda Simoniani, Antitactæ.
Eleemosynas quę pauperibus fiunt, damnant Manichæi, Messaliani.
Omni turpi libidini inseruiunt, & inseruien-dum docent Carpocratiani, Paterniani, Venustiani, Ethicoprocopta.
Opera bona & mala, res esse indifferentes natura, sed opinione hominum tantum distin-gui docent Carpocratiani.
Opera futilia & inania pro causis salutis con-stituunt, veluti utrium gestationem, Ascitæ:
main_text.head: De meritis operum.

page.notes: The "Iustifi-" at the foot is a catchword, not a text line. The "ẃ" flourish before "Manichæi" and the brace before "duo," are printer's ornaments, not text. "eúmque" is printed with an acute over the u, which I have kept as shown. The running head is set in spaced capitals and is transcribed as SYMBOLVM. No page number is printed.
